claim.quote: The DAMA/LIBRA-phase2 data confirm the evidence of a signal that meets all the requirements of the model independent Dark Matter (DM) annual modulation signature, at 9.5 $\sigma$ C.L. in the energy region (1-6) keV.

key_value.quote: a total exposure of 1.13 ton $\times$ yr

name: First model independent results from DAMA/LIBRA-phase2

significance.quote: at 9.5 $\sigma$ C.L. in the energy region (1-6) keV
significance.value: 9.5 sigma C.L. in (1-6) keV; 12.9 sigma C.L. for the full 2.46 ton x yr in (2-6) keV

summary.plain: With new photomultipliers and a lower energy threshold, DAMA/LIBRA-phase2 again found a yearly modulation. The team says it confirms the evidence for dark matter at 9.5 standard deviations, and at 12.9 when all earlier data are included.
summary.technical: Six annual cycles of phase2, exposure 1.13 ton yr, energy threshold 1 keV; 9.5 sigma in 1-6 keV; for the full exposure 2.46 ton yr in 2-6 keV (DAMA/NaI + phase1 + phase2) the C.L. is 12.9 sigma; amplitude (0.0103 +- 0.0008) cpd/kg/keV, phase (145 +- 5) d, period (0.999 +- 0.001) yr.

title: First model independent results from DAMA/LIBRA-phase2
why_it_matters: First results from the upgraded detector, extending the claim to 1 keV; the abstract uses the word 'evidence'.
